# Catalogue Scale — Phase A Baseline

**Date:** 2026-08-25
**Catalogue:** `var/catalog-large.json`, generated by `LargeCatalogGenerator` seed 20260825
**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-25-catalogue-scale-robustness-design.md`
**Plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-25-catalogue-scale-fixture.md`

Reproduce with `ASSISTANT_EVAL_CATALOG=large vendor/bin/phpunit --group eval`. Every number below is
measured. No constant was changed (S7), and nothing under `src/` was touched.

## What was measured against what

Catalogue-side counts, from the product data itself:

| | Small | Large |
|---|---|---|
| Products | 12 | 515 |
| Sellable units | 17 | 2,149 |
| Property groups | 4 | 60 |
| Distinct group/value pairs | 9 | 600 |
| Largest family | 4 variants | 30 variants |

Every constant this kit sets against seventeen units is crossed: `MAX_FIELDS` (30) by 60 groups,
`FACET_VALUE_LIMIT` (50) and `MAX_VALUES_PER_FIELD` (25) by 600 pairs, `MIN_CANDIDATES` (20) and
`MAX_CANDIDATES` (50) by 2,149 units, and the "a family fits the candidate window whole" premise by a
30-variant family.

## What the model is told

`FacetProbe` finds 61 terms fields and 623 values in the large catalogue. This is what survives
`CatalogVocabularyBudget` and reaches the prompt:

| Catalogue | Vocabulary fields | Values | Truncated | Vocabulary chars | Prompt chars |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | 5 | 21 | no | 739 | 3,898 |
| large | **0** | **0** | YES | 561 | 3,720 |

Zero. Not a truncated sample — nothing. See Finding 1.

## Findings

### Finding 1 — the vocabulary block degrades to empty, and says "shortened"

**Observed.** At 2,149 units the block reaches the model with **0 fields and 0 values** while
`truncated` reports `true`. The prompt still carries the instructions around it, so the model is told:

> Words this shop uses. When you search, use these spellings — they are the only spellings this
> catalogue matches […]
>
> (this list is shortened — a word missing from it does not mean the shop lacks it)

with no words between the two. It is not a thin vocabulary; it is an instruction to use a list that
is not there.

**Smallest input that shows it.** **30 property groups**, given field names of the length the DAL
produces (`properties.Colour`, `properties.Manufacturer` — the 30 measured here average 21.9
characters). Because `MAX_FIELDS` is 30, any catalogue with 30 or more groups renders exactly 30
fields, and 30 is one too many: 29 fields at one value each render 1,476 characters and survive, 30
render 1,509 and do not. The mechanism is
`CatalogVocabularyBudget::shrinkToBudget()`, which lowers **one shared per-field value cap** from 25
to 0 and returns the first candidate under `MAX_TOTAL_CHARS` (1500). Measured, at the 30 fields
`MAX_FIELDS` admits:

| Shared value cap | Fields rendered | Rendered chars | Fits 1500? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 30 | 1,998 | no |
| 2 | 30 | 1,752 | no |
| 1 | 30 | **1,509** | no — over by **9** |
| 0 | **0** | 561 | yes |

For comparison, at 29 fields the same shared cap of 1 renders 1,476 characters and fits, so the block
is non-empty. The whole difference between a usable vocabulary and none is one field.

At `cap = 0`, `withValueCap()` filters out every field, because a field with no values is dropped
entirely. So the loop's last step is not "fewer values" but "no vocabulary", and nine characters
decide between the two. This is a cliff, not a gradient: there is no cap between 1 and 0.

**Product or fixture matcher?** **Product.** `FixtureTermMatcher` is not involved — this is
`FacetProbe` → `CatalogVocabulary` → `CatalogVocabularyBudget`, all of it above the gateway, and the
same code path runs against the DAL. A merchant with 30 property groups gets this in production, and
Shopware's own `framework:demodata` seeds 8 groups by default and accepts `--properties=100`.

### Finding 2 — a 30-variant family answers the wrong variant, deterministically

**Observed.** "Endurance Bib Tights, Size 30 — in stock?" renders `sc-family-30-v1` through `v5`. The
requested unit, `sc-family-30-v30`, is never among them: 0/3 runs on both archetypes, six runs, no
exceptions. This is the failure `SearchProductsTool`'s limit docblock records as already having
happened once at `limit: 1`, now reappearing at `DEFAULT_LIMIT = 5` because the family is 30 wide.

**Smallest input that shows it.** A family larger than the limit the model uses, asked about by a
value late in insertion order. Measured through the real tool chain:

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `term: "Endurance Bib Tights", limit: 5` | `v1, v2, v3, v4, v5` |
| `term: "Endurance Bib Tights", limit: 8` | `v1 … v8` |
| `term: "Endurance Bib Tights", options: [["Size","Size 30"]]` | **`v30`, exactly** |

**Product or fixture matcher?** **Product, and ruled in rather than assumed.** Retrieval finds the
right unit the moment the option is supplied, so neither the matcher nor the candidate window is the
constraint. What failed is that the model did not supply the option — and per Finding 1 it was never
told that `Size 30` exists, because the vocabulary block it received was empty. The two findings are
one causal chain, which is why Finding 1 is first.

Note what this is *not*: the candidate window is 20–50 and the family is 30, so the window did hold
the family whole. The trap was aimed at `MIN_CANDIDATES` and caught something upstream of it.

### Finding 3 — a term shared by ~500 products draws "we don't carry"

**Observed.** `scale_broad_term` expert run 3 answered a question about `Trailmaster` — a word carried
by 500 of the 515 products — with "we don't carry". `no_absence_claim_in_prose` caught it, 2/3.
`no_match_not_absence` expert failed the same assertion, 2/3, with "we don't have".

**Smallest input that shows it.** Any term absent from the vocabulary block, which at this scale is
every term. Consistent with Finding 1: a model told "these are the only spellings this catalogue
matches" and handed nothing has no basis for distinguishing "not in the vocabulary" from "not in the
shop". Both failures are the same assertion in the same direction.

**Product or fixture matcher?** **Product.** The absence claim is prose, generated after a search
that did return results.

### Finding 4 — `total` reports the shortlist, not the result set

**Observed.** `SearchProductsTool` returns `'total' => \count($returned)` ([src/Core/Tool/SearchProductsTool.php:340](src/Core/Tool/SearchProductsTool.php#L340)).
Searching `Trailmaster` returns `total: 8` at `limit: 8` against ~500 matching products, with no
`note` in the payload.

**Smallest input that shows it.** Any query matching more products than the limit. At 17 units the
shortlist usually *is* the result set, so the field name is accurate there; at 500 matches it is off
by two orders of magnitude and nothing in the reply says so.

**Product or fixture matcher?** **Product** — it is the tool's own return shape. Whether the model
should be told the true match count is a design question, not a bug, which is why
`scale_broad_term` deliberately asserts nothing about it. Recorded here because it is the premise the
card row rests on, and at scale it is a claim rather than a given.

### Finding 5 — not determined: the deep-duplicate expert archetype

`scale_deep_duplicate · expert` rendered only `sc-deep-duplicate`, missing both `fx-007` and `fx-008`,
0/3. No probe reproduces that set: the verbatim name returns `fx-007, sc-deep-duplicate`, the term
`750ml` returns the same, and `limit: 1` returns `fx-007` alone. The term the model actually searched
is not recoverable from the eval's summary output, so the mechanism is unknown.

What *is* established is the tokenisation fact behind the assertion's difficulty: `fx-008` is "Alloy
Water Bottle 750 ml" and the matcher finds no `750ml` substring in `750 ml`, so a verbatim-name search
reaches two of the three by construction. That part is the fixture matcher, not the product, and it is
why this journey's expectation is the most brittle of the four. **This one needs the trace before it
is called anything.**

## What this does not say

**Retrieval quality at scale.** `FixtureTermMatcher` is substring matching with an all-tokens pass and
an any-token fallback — no keyword index, no relevance ranking, no `slop()` prefix generation, and
therefore none of the plural blind spot that produced the `gloves` defect. Every number above
describes the layers above the gateway.

**The two flaky existing failures may be the matcher getting broader.** `injection_discount · beginner`
rendered `gen-0361-*` where it expected `fx-017`; filler products matching a query is exactly what the
any-token fallback does more of at 515 products than at 12. Not established either way — and per the
spec, a finding that cannot say which cause it has is not a finding yet. Both are listed in the table
and deliberately absent from *Findings*.

**Single runs.** Findings 1, 2 and 4 are deterministic — arithmetic, or 0/3 across six runs. Finding 3
rests on 1 of 3 runs in each of two journeys. One run is an anecdote; the direction is consistent
across two independent journeys, which is why it is recorded, but the rate is not measured.

**Nothing below the gateway.** No latency, no query count, no aggregation behaviour, no `FACET_VALUE_LIMIT`
actually capping anything — the fixture gateway has no such cap, so `sc-rare-option` tested whether a
rare value survives an empty vocabulary (it did, 3/3) rather than whether a 50-bucket aggregation can
return it. That is phase B's half.

## Recommended next step

**A fix plan for Finding 1, before phase B.**

The reasoning: Finding 1 is deterministic, sits entirely above the gateway, is reproducible without a
model or a database, and is the demonstrated cause of Finding 2 and the likely cause of Finding 3.
Phase B measures latency and query counts below the gateway — it would not observe this, and its
numbers would be gathered against a prompt that is empty for the wrong reason. Measuring a shop while
a known upstream defect distorts every turn buys numbers that have to be taken again afterwards.

Finding 1 is also cheap to fix and cheap to test: the failing test is a `CatalogVocabularyBudget` unit
test asserting that 31 groups produce a non-empty block, and it needs no LLM. Findings 2 and 3 should
be re-measured after it, since both may resolve without their own fix — `scale_family_beyond_window`
is the direct check and already exists.

S7 stands: **no constant was tuned here.** The cliff in Finding 1 is not a case for a bigger
`MAX_TOTAL_CHARS` — raising 1500 moves the cliff without removing it. What the measurement argues for
is that the last step of `shrinkToBudget()` should degrade to fewer *fields* with values rather than to
no fields at all. That is a fix plan's decision to make, with its own failing test, not this report's.
